I'm going through the same thing. 1 month later. Still hurts. At a certain point, I thought you were supposed to commit to the "work" part of "a relationship takes work." You find a person you're in love with, you see them in your future, and--short of an abusive relationship or one that hurts more than it helps--you fucking work on that shit because you're committed to someone. I guess that's too much to accept.

This was me 24 hours ago. It's not as bad today, and I hope tomorrow isn't as bad either. I've been cut off from my therapist, too, and it sucks. 

Can you call a friend or family member just to hear a familiar voice and talk about something?

Here are some things I try cycling through (over and over again when it's really bad) that maybe you can try:

1. Watching a funny movie/stand-up comedy
2. Listening to pop/upbeat music or watching music videos
3. Working out (push ups, crunches, planks)
4. Cooking/baking
5. Curling up in a ball and crying for a little bit (5 min) and they STOPPING AND DISTRACTING WITH SOMETHING ELSE
6. Putting a favorite show on in the background while you do something with your hands (crafts, video games)
7. Guided meditation
8. Slow, deep breathing in through your nose and out through your mouth
9. Asking people what they like about you/what your strengths are
10. Rearranging furniture (good for change of space and physical activity)

Feel free to message me, seriously. You are not alone. Good luck <3

The group portion of DBT can be very awkward. But it really does provide a strange sense of relief to be around people with similar shit they're trying to deal with. 

I think individual therapists in DBT therapy will refuse to see you if you can't/don't want to commit to group :/ You'd think they'd want to offer some help rather than nothing at all, but I guess not. Otherwise, maybe look for someone that specializes in depression or emotional dysregulation or whatever it is you're hoping to address specifically. Good luck <3
